title: Ossobuco alla Milanese
subtitle: Braised veal shin with gremolata
excerpt: Cross-cut veal shanks braised slowly in white wine and stock until the meat falls from the bone. Finished with gremolata, a mixture of lemon zest, garlic, and parsley, stirred in at the very end. Traditionally served with saffron risotto.

recipe.sourceNotes: Ossobuco means bone with a hole, a reference to the marrow-filled cross-cut of the shin. The dish is a staple of Milanese cooking, first documented in the nineteenth century. The authentic Milanese version is made without tomato (ossobuco in bianco); the tomato version became more widespread in the twentieth century. The gremolata is not optional, it provides the brightness that cuts through the richness of the braise.

recipeTools.notes: Heavy braising pot with a lid.

content.text: Ossobuco is one of the great Italian braises. The only tricky part is browning the veal shanks properly, they are thick pieces and need high heat and patience to develop a proper crust without steaming. Tie each shank with kitchen twine before browning to stop the meat falling off the bone. The marrow in the centre of each bone is part of the dish; scoop it out with a narrow spoon and eat it on a slice of bread with salt.

items.preparation: cross-cut, each about 300 g, tied with twine

content.text: Season the veal shanks and dust lightly in flour. Heat the oil in a heavy pot over high heat. Brown the shanks for 4 minutes per side until deep golden. Remove and set aside.
Reduce to medium. Add the butter, onion, celery, and carrot. Cook for 10 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits. Reduce by half.

Return the shanks to the pot. Add the stock, bay leaves, and thyme. The liquid should come halfway up the shanks. Cover and cook on a very low heat, barely simmering, for 1.5 to 2 hours until the meat is completely tender and pulling from the bone.

Mix together the lemon zest, minced garlic, and parsley for the gremolata. Remove the twine from the shanks. Taste the sauce for salt and pepper. Scatter the gremolata over and serve with saffron risotto.
